analysis:
Examined SSDPrefixCache.swift base lines 1–1255 and the eviction patch at base 1772–1787/head 1772–1779 against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. The supplied source preserves salt-bound chain hashes/HMAC tags, weight/layout metadata bindings, donation benefit and size gates, write-rate/queue limits, sliding freshness updates, request-specific adoption tickets and per-entry reservation release. These excerpts are unchanged according to the complete range map; their existing limitations are not PR findings. No changes to authorization, attestation, wire encryption, billing or plaintext logging are shown.
The actual change adds a closed-cache guard and delegates the oldest-entry iteration to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, retaining retireIndexedEntries as the removal callback and counting an eviction only when bytes are freed (head 1772–1779). No concrete regression is established. Integration must inspect the new helper and its interaction with SSDDiskBudget and retireIndexedEntries: preserve bounded iteration, skip undeletable victims, stop on external storage change, report only indexed bytes actually freed, and avoid removals after closure. This contract is material to T-041's disk-budget/storage mitigations and availability, but the helper and retirement implementation are outside these supplied source units; delegation alone does not prove they are missing controls.
